\subsection{What is counted, and what cannot be}\label{sec:stats-method}

\textbf{Counted, exactly.} Every figure in this section is a count of an artifact that exists in one of the two repositories at the snapshot instant: a JSON record in \texttt{.frontier/log.jsonl}, a ledger entry under \texttt{proofs/*/ledger/}, a front-matter field in an \texttt{argument/lemmas/*.md} or \texttt{definitions/*.md} shard, a directory under \texttt{runs/} or \texttt{docs/}, a heading in \texttt{docs/worklog.md} or \texttt{FINDINGS.md}, a record in \texttt{.beads/issues.jsonl}, or a commit in \texttt{git log}. No figure is modelled, interpolated, or extrapolated.

\textbf{Not recoverable: LLM token consumption.} The single most-asked statistic about a campaign like this one --- how many tokens, and at what cost --- is \emph{not} present in the record and is not reconstructed here. Neither repository ever logged token counts, context sizes, wall-clock durations, or billing data; the \texttt{af} ledger records who claimed which node and when, not how much text was produced to do it, and the \texttt{fr} log records a worker's \texttt{model:role} pair, not its usage. What \emph{is} recoverable is the \emph{job} count --- how many distinct prover/verifier invocations were made --- and that is reported exactly in \Cref{sec:stats-workers}. Multiplying a job count by a guessed per-job token figure would produce a number with no evidentiary basis, so it is omitted rather than invented (\textsc{claude.md} L0/L3: a number without a re-run command is not a finding).

\textbf{Other honest gaps.}
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{0.15ex}
\item The progenitor repository predates the \texttt{fr} controller, so it has no cycle/arm/outcome record at all. Its exploration history is reconstructible only from 22 work-log entries and 174 commits, at coarser granularity than this repository's 1\,143 controller cycles.
\item The progenitor repository's issue tracker is stored in an embedded Dolt database rather than an exported \texttt{issues.jsonl}, so its issue counts are not in this snapshot.
\item \texttt{fr} evidence records carry a self-reported \texttt{verdict} field whose value is \texttt{claimed} on every one of the 519 records that has one. It is a protocol marker, not an adjudication, and is therefore not tabulated as an outcome.
\item Wave numbering (\texttt{W1}--\texttt{W134}) is a human convention in the work log and wave documents; it is not a controller-enforced counter, and a few numbers were skipped or reused. Counts of wave \emph{documents} are exact; the wave \emph{index} is indicative.
\item Cross-repository carry-over (what this campaign inherited from the progenitor) is described qualitatively in \Cref{sec:stats-progenitor}; it is a judgement about content, not a count.
\end{itemize}


\subsection{The campaign calendar}\label{sec:stats-calendar}

\subsection{The rigour ladder}\label{sec:stats-ladder}

The project's whole point is that a claim's \emph{status} is tracked honestly and separately from its plausibility. The registry therefore carries a status census, and the only rung that counts as rigorous in-repo is an \texttt{af}-validated tree (or a byte-matched citation). Of 365 registry results, 170 carry \texttt{af: validated} --- 46.6\% of the registry. The remainder are flagged non-rigorous in the open.

\subsection{The exploration controller: arms and outcomes}\label{sec:stats-arms}

Research directions are registered as \texttt{fr} \emph{arms}; every harvested result is logged as one pull with an outcome, and a Stop-hook circuit-breaker forces a stalled arm to yield. Across 1\,143 cycles, 773 carried an arm label and 370 were orientation or bookkeeping records. The controller recorded 522 explicit allocation decisions: \texttt{EXPLOIT} $\times$ 505, \texttt{EXPLORE} $\times$ 14, \texttt{PIVOT} $\times$ 3.

\subsection{Adversarial elevations}\label{sec:stats-elevations}

A result reaches the top in-repo rung only through an \texttt{af} workspace: the registry contract becomes the root conjecture, a fresh prover agent builds a proof tree, and every node is validated by a \emph{separate} fresh verifier told that finding a gap is a success. The orchestrator never judges a step. 184 workspaces were opened; 172 reached a validated root and 12 remain seeded or open. Between them the workers built 2\,526 proof nodes, raised 415 challenges (of which 406 were resolved), and forced 351 node amendments.

\subsection{Worker and job census}\label{sec:stats-workers}

Two independent records count delegated work. The \texttt{fr} log names the workers involved in each harvested cycle as \texttt{model:role} pairs; that is a curated, human-entered field and covers 524 worker mentions across 37 distinct model/role pairs. The \texttt{af} ledgers count \emph{invocations} mechanically: every \texttt{nodes\_claimed} entry is one worker taking one node, and the claim's owner string encodes whether it was the initial prover build, a prover fix round, or a verifier pass. \subsection{Progenitor and successor}\label{sec:stats-progenitor}

The classical portfolio was not born here. It began as a side-quest inside \texttt{almost-\discretionary{}{}{}idempotent-\discretionary{}{}{}positive-\discretionary{}{}{}maps}, whose own target was the non-commutative problem; the classical case was its proving ground. That campaign ran 2026-06-02 to 2026-06-13 (174 commits, 22 work-log entries) and reached 59 registry results with 16 \texttt{af}-validated roots across 16 workspaces and 132 proof nodes. This repository was stood up 2026-07-02 --- 19 days later --- specifically to re-establish the classical result from scratch under a stricter ladder.

\textbf{What carried over.} Three things, and each was re-tagged \emph{down} on arrival:
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{0.15ex}
\item \textbf{The reduction chain.} The progenitor reduced the classical stability statement, through audited and audit-pending steps, to a single open kernel (the ``(EX)'' conjecture). The chain re-entered this repository as \texttt{stated} or \texttt{proved-mod-audit} --- objects of study, not oracles --- and 22 of the 365 registry results here still carry that inherited tag.
\item \textbf{The numerical record.} The 67{,}000-instance exact enumeration and the seed experiments were copied wholesale into \texttt{docs/ingest/} (60 files) and re-homed as run bundles. Their status did not change: \texttt{numerical}, L3, never rigorous.
\item \textbf{One validated result.} Exactly one classical result had cleared an \texttt{af} validation upstream --- \texttt{lem-classical-equiv}, the signed$\leftrightarrow$stochastic bridge. It was nevertheless re-validated here from scratch (29 nodes, 6 challenges) and that in-repo run, not the upstream one, is what this repository's ladder rests on.
\end{itemize}

In throughput terms the successor is roughly 6.5 times the progenitor in commits, 6.2 times in registry size, and 10.8 times in \texttt{af}-validated results, over 2.9 times the elapsed span.


\subsection{Colophon: how this section stays true}\label{sec:stats-colophon}

Everything in \Cref{sec:campaign-statistics} is generated by \texttt{scripts/gen-report-stats.py} into \texttt{report/generated/stats/}. The shard in \texttt{report/sections/} contains no numbers; it only \texttt{\textbackslash input}s the generated body.

\textbf{The staleness problem.} Statistics about a repository depend on things that change with every commit --- git history, the controller log, the proof ledgers. A byte-for-byte freshness gate over such a generator would be permanently red, because the very commit that lands the regenerated tables changes their inputs again. The generator therefore runs in two halves with a committed snapshot between them:

\begin{quote}\footnotesize\raggedright
\texttt{python3 scripts/gen-report-stats.py --extract}\par
\hspace*{1.5em}mines the live sources into \texttt{report/generated/stats/campaign-extract.json} \emph{and} re-renders.\par\smallskip
\texttt{python3 scripts/gen-report-stats.py}\par
\hspace*{1.5em}renders the \texttt{.tex} files from that committed snapshot, deterministically.\par\smallskip
\texttt{python3 scripts/gen-report-stats.py --check}\par
\hspace*{1.5em}the gate: re-renders, byte-compares, and prints a non-fatal drift advisory.
\end{quote}

\textbf{Staleness semantics.} Only the render step is gated, so the check is stable across ordinary commits and fails exactly when it should: a hand-edited generated file, or a renderer change without a re-render. The \emph{numbers}, by contrast, are as of \textbf{2026-08-05T12:05:57Z} and go stale silently by design --- refreshing them is a deliberate act. \texttt{--check} therefore also compares a few cheap live counts against the snapshot and prints how far behind it is, without blocking a commit.

\textbf{Progenitor data.} The \texttt{almost-\discretionary{}{}{}idempotent-\discretionary{}{}{}positive-\discretionary{}{}{}maps} block is mined live when that repository sits beside this one and is otherwise carried forward from the committed snapshot, so the gate is green on machines that do not have the sibling. The current block was mined live at the last extraction.

\textbf{Provenance of the figures.} 1\,143 controller records, 15\,502 \texttt{af} ledger entries, 365 registry shards, 47 definition shards, 38 run bundles, 81 work-log entries, 210 issue records, and 1\,298 commits were read to produce this section.
